title: Psalm 60: Have You Rejected Us, O God?
summary: Israel has suffered a military disaster, and the people cry out that God has rejected them and shaken the land. At the center of the psalm God answers from his sanctuary, claiming the tribes of Israel as his own and the surrounding nations as his servants. The psalm ends with a plea for help against Edom and the confidence that with God the people will act with valor.

from.where: The Study Bible's notes on Psalm 60

line: After a defeat the people cry that God has rejected them; God answers from his sanctuary, and the psalm ends trusting that with God they will act with valor.
guide: It teaches a people what to do after a defeat: tell God the truth, listen for his promise, and go on with him. Ask where you have been broken, and pray verse 12 there.

stanzas.title: The land shaken and the people staggered
A banner for those who fear God, and a plea for rescue
God's oracle: the land is Mine, the nations serve Me
Who will lead us to Edom?
Human help is worthless; with God we will prevail

verses.t: For the choirmaster. To the tune of “The Lily of the Covenant.” A Miktam of David for instruction. When he fought Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab returned and struck down 12,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. You have rejected us, O God; You have broken us; You have been angry; restore us!
You have shaken the land and torn it open. Heal its fractures, for it is quaking.
You have shown Your people hardship; we are staggered from the wine You made us drink.
You have raised a banner for those who fear You, that they may flee the bow. Selah
Respond and save us with Your right hand, that Your beloved may be delivered.
God has spoken from His sanctuary: “I will triumph! I will parcel out Shechem and apportion the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is Mine, and Manasseh is Mine; Ephraim is My helmet, Judah is My scepter.
Moab is My washbasin; upon Edom I toss My sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Have You not rejected us, O God? Will You no longer march out, O God, with our armies?
Give us aid against the enemy, for the help of man is worthless.
With God we will perform with valor, and He will trample our enemies.
